Jerome Ghost Town Tour: Your Complete Guide to Arizona's Haunted Hill

Perched precariously on Cleopatra Hill, Jerome is Arizona's most famous ghost town — though with a few hundred year-round residents, it's more accurately described as a "living ghost town." Once home to thousands of copper miners, this former boomtown now draws visitors with its history, arts scene, quirky shops, and yes, reported hauntings. A Jerome day trip from Phoenix is one of Arizona's most unique adventures.

The short answer: a Jerome day is priced by the hour, with free hours on long days. An 8-hour trip on the Luxury SUV (6 seats, $125/hr) bills 7 hours: $875 before tax, about $146 per person. A 12-hour Jerome-plus-Sedona day on the Executive Sprinter (14 seats, $145/hr) bills 10 hours: $1,450, about $104 per person. Book it as our Jerome and Prescott tour.

Understanding Jerome

The Basics

  • Location: 100 miles north of Phoenix, near Prescott
  • Elevation: 5,066 feet (Cleopatra Hill)
  • Population: a few hundred year-round residents
  • Founded: 1876 (copper mining town)
  • Nickname: "The Largest Ghost Town in America"

The History

Jerome boomed during the copper mining era:

  • 1876: First claims staked
  • 1880s-1950s: Active mining operations
  • Peak population: many thousands of residents
  • 1953: Mines closed
  • Population dropped to a few dozen
  • 1967: Designated a National Historic Landmark
  • Today: Artists' colony and tourist destination

The Ghost Stories

Jerome is famous for its alleged hauntings:

  • Jerome Grand Hotel (former hospital)
  • The Connor Hotel
  • The Sliding Jail (moved by ground shifting from mine blasting)
  • Various Main Street buildings
  • Ghost tours operate in the evenings

Getting to Jerome

The Route Options

From Phoenix via I-17 (Faster):

  • Distance: 100 miles
  • Route: I-17 to Cordes Junction → AZ-69 to Prescott Valley → AZ-89A to Jerome
  • Pros: Faster, less winding
  • Cons: Less scenic

From Phoenix via I-17 and AZ-260 (Scenic):

  • Distance: about 110 miles
  • Route: I-17 to Camp Verde → AZ-260 to Cottonwood → AZ-89A up the hill to Jerome
  • Pros: Verde Valley views, wine country on the way
  • Cons: Longer, more curves

Why Professional Transportation?

The Roads:
AZ-89A between Cottonwood and Jerome (or Prescott and Jerome) is famously winding with:

  • Hairpin turns
  • Steep grades
  • Dramatic drop-offs
  • No guardrails in places

The Experience:
You want to look at the views, not focus on driving. Let us handle the curves while you enjoy the scenery.

Wine Tasting:
Jerome has wine tasting rooms. A designated driver is essential.

What to Do in Jerome

Historical Attractions

Jerome State Historic Park

  • Located in the Douglas Mansion
  • Copper mining history exhibits
  • Town history and photographs
  • Stunning valley views

Gold King Mine & Ghost Town

  • Just outside Jerome
  • Antique machinery, vehicles
  • Actual ghost town ruins
  • Great for photographers

The Sliding Jail

  • Slid downhill after mine blasting shifted the ground
  • Historic landmark
  • Photo opportunity

Ghost & Paranormal

Jerome Grand Hotel

  • Formerly the United Verde Hospital
  • Alleged hotspot for paranormal activity
  • Ghost tours available
  • Asylum Restaurant on premises

Ghost Tours:

  • Several operators offer evening tours
  • 1-2 hour walking tours
  • History meets hauntings

Shopping & Art

Main Street Galleries:

  • Working artists' studios
  • Local and Native American art
  • Unique jewelry and crafts

Quirky Shops:

  • Haunted-themed merchandise
  • Antiques and collectibles
  • Local crafts

Wine Tasting

Jerome has a small but growing wine scene:

  • Caduceus Cellars
  • Jerome Winery
  • Cellar 433

Seasonal Considerations

Spring (March-May)

  • Weather: Mild, 60s-70s
  • Crowds: Moderate
  • Best For: Comfortable exploring

Summer (June-August)

  • Weather: Warm but not Phoenix-hot (80s)
  • Crowds: Heavy (tourists + day-trippers)
  • Best For: Cooler escape

Fall (September-November)

  • Weather: Perfect (60s-70s)
  • Crowds: Moderate
  • Best For: Fall colors, ideal weather

Winter (December-February)

  • Weather: Cold (40s-50s), occasional snow
  • Crowds: Light
  • Best For: Fewer crowds, atmospheric

Jerome Day Trip FAQ

Q: Is Jerome really haunted?
A: That's for you to decide. The town's history — mining accidents, hospital deaths — provides plenty of stories. Several TV shows have investigated.

Q: How much time do I need in Jerome?
A: 3-4 hours covers the highlights. A full day allows deeper exploration.

Q: Can I combine Jerome with Sedona?
A: Absolutely — it's a popular combination. The drive between them is stunning, and the 12-hour day earns two free hours.

Q: Is the drive to Jerome difficult?
A: AZ-89A has significant curves and elevation change. Our drivers are experienced with these roads.

Q: Are there restrooms and food in Jerome?
A: Yes, multiple restaurants and public facilities.

Q: What's the cancellation policy?
A: Cancellation terms depend on your date and booking; read the cancellation policy before you book. One free date change at 72+ hours. See our policies page.
